cards.Name: Alert
cards.note: not a concrete noun; overlaps Alarm

cards.Name: Angel
cards.note: Islamic: angels should not be depicted/drawn

cards.Name: Armour
cards.note: Debate: British spelling, as used in Pakistan and in the earlier Odour fix.

cards.Name: Medal
cards.note: Debate: Award means the same as the live Prize card and overlaps Trophy. Medal keeps the winning idea and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Crispy Chicken
cards.note: not a single noun; duplicate of Chicken (game12-112)

cards.Name: Life Jacket
cards.note: Debate: Swimsuit is too close to the banned bikini for a family audience. Life Jacket keeps the water idea, is not in the deck and is easy to act out.

cards.Name: Kidney
cards.note: Debate: Bladder invites the toilet jokes the owner banned. Kidney keeps the body-organ slot and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Hot Air Balloon
cards.note: Debate: A blimp is little known in Pakistan. Hot Air Balloon is familiar, easy to draw and different from Balloon.

cards.Name: Blackboard
cards.note: Debate: 'Board' is too vague. Blackboard is concrete, familiar from school, and not already in the deck.

cards.Name: Booger
cards.note: Debate: Means the same as Snot, which is live (game12-559), and is the cruder of the two.

cards.Name: Bunny
cards.note: Debate: Means the same as Rabbit, which is live (game12-812).

cards.Name: Toffee
cards.note: Debate: Candy overlaps the live Candy Bar and Candy Wrapper cards and is the US word. Toffee is the local word and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Eid Card
cards.note: Debate: 'Card' is vague and reads as playing cards. Eid Card is concrete and local, and it is different from Eidi and Credit Card.

cards.Name: Charm
cards.note: ambiguous; amulet/charm conflicts with Islamic content

cards.Name: Chilli
cards.note: Debate: Standard Pakistani/British spelling, and it avoids the US 'chili' stew sense. The deck's own spelling is mixed (Rumor alongside Armour/Odour).

cards.Name: Cupboard
cards.note: Debate: Closet is the US word; Cupboard is the local word and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Cookie
cards.note: Debate: Same meaning as Biscuit for Pakistani players; Cookie Jar and Cookie Tin stay in the deck.

cards.Name: Couch
cards.note: Debate: Same meaning as the live Sofa card; Sofa is the usual Pakistani word.

cards.Name: Metal Detector
cards.note: Debate: Detector alone is vague; Metal Detector is a clear object and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Water Dispenser
cards.note: Debate: Dispenser alone is vague; Water Dispenser is common and different enough from Cooler.

cards.Name: Dustbin
cards.note: Sweep: US term (dumpster) replaced with local word

cards.Name: Tap
cards.note: Debate: Faucet is the US word; Tap is the local word and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Film
cards.note: western/secular (film/pop culture); also duplicate of Movie

cards.Name: Fluid
cards.note: vague, hard to describe or draw

cards.Name: Salan
cards.note: Debate: Gravy nearly duplicates Sauce (idx 513). Salan is a distinct, everyday Pakistani dish and is not yet in the deck.

cards.Name: Jewel
cards.note: Debate: Same meaning as Gem (idx 246); the deck also has Jewelry, Diamond and Pearl.

cards.Name: Charpai
cards.note: Sweep: US cowboy item (lasso) replaced with local noun

cards.Name: Mist
cards.note: Debate: Near-duplicate of Fog, which is in the deck. Players cannot tell the two apart when describing or acting.

cards.Name: Mitten
cards.note: Debate: Near-duplicate of Glove, which is in the deck, and uncommon in Pakistan.

cards.Name: Musket
cards.note: Debate: Obscure historical weapon. Gun and Cannon in the deck already cover it.

cards.Name: Moustache
cards.note: Debate: British/Pakistani spelling matches the deck's style. No other card says Moustache.

cards.Name: Pyjamas
cards.note: Debate: British/Pakistani spelling matches the deck's style (Armour, Odour). No other card says Pyjamas.

cards.Name: Toothpaste
cards.note: Debate: 'Paste' is vague; Toothpaste is clear, drawable and not already in the deck

cards.Name: Plunger
cards.note: Debate: Toilet tool that invites bathroom jokes, which the owner disallows. The deck already has Toilet.

cards.Name: Raincoat
cards.note: Debate: Poncho is uncommon in Pakistan. Raincoat keeps the same idea and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Gola Ganda
cards.note: Debate: Popsicle is a US word that overlaps Kulfi, Ice Cream and Ice Cream Stick. Gola Ganda is the local equivalent and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Stethoscope
cards.note: Debate: Probe is vague and hard to act or draw. Stethoscope is concrete and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Rage
cards.note: Debate: Synonym of Anger, which is in the deck.

cards.Name: Abaya
cards.note: Debate: Robe overlaps Gown and Cloak. Abaya is a familiar local garment and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Mela
cards.note: Sweep: US-only (rodeo) replaced with local noun

cards.Name: Rubber
cards.note: Debate: In Pakistani English it means eraser, which duplicates Eraser. It also overlaps Rubber Band and Rubber Stamp.

cards.Name: Rumour
cards.note: Debate: Uses the British spelling found in Pakistani English, matching Armour and Odour already in the deck.

cards.Name: Sculpture
cards.note: Debate: Near-synonym of Statue, which is in the deck.

cards.Name: Samosa
cards.note: Sweep: Mexican/US food (taco) replaced with local noun

cards.Name: Tie
cards.note: Debate: Same meaning as the live Necktie card.

cards.Name: Tikka
cards.note: Debate: Tofu is little known in Pakistan. Tikka is a familiar local food and is not in the deck; Kebab is a different word.

cards.Name: Toilet
cards.note: Debate: The owner's later decisions ban bathroom/toilet jokes, and drawing or acting this word invites them.

cards.Name: Tumour
cards.note: Debate: The live deck already uses British spelling (Armour, Odour, Rumour). Tumor is the US spelling.

cards.Name: TV
cards.note: abbreviation capitalized; kept over later Television (game12-723)

cards.Name: Vapour
cards.note: Debate: Matches the deck's British spelling (Armour, Odour, Rumour).

cards.Name: Toilet Paper Tube
cards.note: Debate: The owner has ruled out toilet jokes, and this card mainly invites them. It also overlaps Tube (662) and Tissues (731).

cards.Name: Matchbox
cards.note: Debate: In a cricket-mad group, 'Matches' could mean games. Matchbox (maachis) is clear, easy to draw and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Washcloth
cards.note: Debate: A Western bathroom item, covered by Towel and Sponge, which are both live.

cards.Name: Incense Stick
cards.note: clearer/standard spelling: was Stick Of Incense

cards.Name: Dice
cards.note: clearer/standard spelling: was Pair Of Dice

cards.Name: Pepper Shaker
cards.note: Debate: Salt Shaker and Pepper are both live. This card adds nothing new.

cards.Name: Jam Jar
cards.note: clearer/standard spelling: was Jar Of Jam

cards.Name: Pickle Jar
cards.note: Debate: Pickle and Jar are both live. This is the same kind of combined duplicate as Pearl Necklace.

cards.Name: Razai
cards.note: Debate: Razai is the familiar desi word for a quilt, and no Razai card exists. It is distinct from Blanket.

cards.Name: Pearl Necklace
cards.note: Debate: Pearl and Necklace are both live. This is just the two cards combined.

cards.Name: Egg Timer
cards.note: Debate: Hourglass and Clock are live. This is a redundant Western kitchen variant.

cards.Name: Jigsaw Puzzle
cards.note: Debate: Duplicate of Puzzle, which is live.

cards.Name: Pagri
cards.note: Sweep: US-only (cowboy hat) replaced with local noun

cards.Name: Baseball Cap
cards.note: Debate: US-centric. Cap, Hat and Topi are all live.

cards.Name: Flashlight
cards.note: Debate: Duplicate of Torch, which is live and is the local term.

cards.Name: Cookie Tin
cards.note: Debate: A near-duplicate of Cookie Jar and Tin Can, which are both live.

cards.Name: Hair Ribbon
cards.note: Debate: Ribbon, Hair Tie and Paranda are all live.

cards.Name: Multitool
cards.note: Debate: A niche gadget that is hard to act out. Pocket Knife is live.

cards.Name: Masking Tape
cards.note: Debate: Duplicate of Tape, which is live.

cards.Name: Toe Ring
cards.note: Debate: A compound of the live cards Toe and Ring, and mainly a Hindu bridal custom.

cards.Name: Steak Knife
cards.note: Debate: A Western variant. Knife and Pocket Knife are live.

cards.Name: Craft Book
cards.note: Debate: A vague compound. Book, Notebook, Comic Book and Sketch Pad are all live.

cards.Name: Can Of Peas
cards.note: Debate: Can of Beans and Tin Can are both live, so this is a duplicate.

cards.Name: Can of Beans
cards.note: Debate: Near-duplicate of Tin Can; Western baked-beans pantry item

cards.Name: Lemon
cards.note: Debate: Indistinguishable from the live Lime card (both nimbu) when drawn or acted

cards.Name: Cookie Jar
cards.note: Debate: Duplicates Jar, Jam Jar and Cookie; matches earlier removal of Cookie Tin

cards.Name: Whipped Cream
cards.note: Debate: Duplicates Cream and Ice Cream and is a Western dessert topping; renaming it Malai would just be another Cream duplicate

cards.Name: Jar of Peanut Butter
cards.note: Debate: A phrase rather than a single noun, duplicates Jar/Jam Jar, and is US-centric

cards.Name: Rusty Nail
cards.note: dup of Nail (811); also a cocktail name

cards.Name: Shalwar Kameez
cards.note: New card; Debate: The full national dress is a standard compound noun and easier to act out or draw than the trousers alone

cards.Name: Bangles
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar local accessory, distinct from Bracelet. Not in the live deck.

cards.Name: Chai
cards.note: New card (debate): The national drink. The live deck has only Teapot and Kettle, no Tea or Chai card.

cards.Name: Shuttlecock
cards.note: New card (debate): Common local game item. There is no badminton, racket or shuttle card in the live deck.

cards.Name: Gilli Danda
cards.note: New card (debate): Classic South Asian street game that is good to act out. Not in the live deck.

cards.Name: Pressure Cooker
cards.note: New card (debate): Found in every desi kitchen, and its whistle is easy to act out. There is no cooker card in the live deck.

cards.Name: Wheelbarrow
cards.note: New card (debate): Concrete, easy-to-draw noun known everywhere. There is no wheelbarrow or cart card in the live deck.

cards.Name: Crocodile
cards.note: New card (debate): Well-known animal; neither Crocodile nor Alligator is in the deck.

cards.Name: Earthquake
cards.note: New card (debate): Easy to act out and relevant locally; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Exam
cards.note: New card (debate): Relatable; neither Exam nor Test is in the deck.

cards.Name: Fridge
cards.note: New card (debate): Everyday object; neither Fridge nor Refrigerator is in the deck.

cards.Name: Firecracker
cards.note: New card (debate): The owner allows fireworks; no Firecracker or Fireworks card exists.

cards.Name: Chulha
cards.note: New card (debate): A well-known Pakistani household word that fits Tandoor, Tawa and Handi; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Cradle
cards.note: New card (debate): Drawable object; neither Cradle nor Crib is in the deck.

cards.Name: Eclipse
cards.note: New card (debate): Drawable sky event; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Calculator
cards.note: New card (debate): Common, easy to draw; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Chandelier
cards.note: New card (debate): Easy to draw and common in shaadi halls; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Miswak
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar Sunnah tooth-cleaning stick, easy to act out, and not in the deck. Floss (idx 221) is a valid dental noun and stays as it is (challenger's amendment).

cards.Name: Hiccup
cards.note: New card (debate): Easy to act out and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Jinn
cards.note: New card (debate): The owner allows jinn jokes; not in the deck (no Jinn or Genie).

cards.Name: Ghee
cards.note: New card (debate): Everyday Pakistani kitchen noun that is also standard English; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Garlic
cards.note: New card (debate): Common concrete noun that is easy to draw; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Falcon
cards.note: New card (debate): The shaheen is well known in Pakistan; the deck has no falcon, eagle or hawk.

cards.Name: Chowkidar
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar local figure that is fun to act out; no Guard or Watchman in the deck.

cards.Name: Hand Pump
cards.note: New card (debate): The village nalka, easy to draw. The standard two-word spelling keeps it distinct from the existing Pump card (challenger's amendment).

cards.Name: Cart
cards.note: New card (debate): Street vendor's cart (thela) or hand cart. It is an English word, so it suits this all-English deck better than 'Thela' (challenger's amendment). Not in the deck: only Game Cartridge and Carton of Ice Cream are.

cards.Name: Hail
cards.note: New card (debate): Weather noun to go with Fog, Hurricane and the others; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Gate
cards.note: New card (debate): Simple everyday noun that is easy to draw; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Lunchbox
cards.note: Debate: Means the same as 'Tiffin' (idx 1025), so clues would be identical; keep Tiffin, which has the local flavour.

cards.Name: Lollipop
cards.note: New card (debate): Distinct, drawable treat; not in deck

cards.Name: Microwave
cards.note: New card (debate): Common kitchen appliance; not in deck

cards.Name: Passport
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar object, good for describing; not in deck

cards.Name: Pakol
cards.note: New card (debate): Iconic Chitrali/Pashtun cap, local frame; not in deck

cards.Name: Parcel
cards.note: New card (debate): Everyday delivery noun, easy to mime; not in deck

cards.Name: Mosquito Coil
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar Pakistani household item, distinct from Mosquito; not in deck

cards.Name: Muezzin
cards.note: New card (debate): Owner-allowed respectful person noun (gives the azan); not in deck

cards.Name: Penguin
cards.note: New card (debate): Popular, actable animal; not in deck

cards.Name: Lighthouse
cards.note: New card (debate): Distinctive drawable object; not in deck

cards.Name: Pulao
cards.note: New card (debate): Everyday Pakistani dish, distinct from Biryani, and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Raita
cards.note: New card (debate): Common side dish; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Qawwali
cards.note: New card (debate): The owner explicitly allows it, and it is easy to act out; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Shikanjvi
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar summer lemon drink; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Saag
cards.note: New card (debate): Well-known Punjabi dish; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Sadqa
cards.note: New card (debate): Common, respectful Islamic concept; neither Charity nor Zakat is in the deck.

cards.Name: Rishta
cards.note: New card (debate): A family marriage proposal, not romance; fits with Baraat and Mehndi and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Roza
cards.note: New card (debate): Pairs with Iftar; accurate and respectful; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Pateela
cards.note: New card (debate): Common cooking pot that is easy to draw; only Handi, Teapot and Clay Pot are in the deck.

cards.Name: Paranda
cards.note: New card (debate): Concrete traditional hair accessory; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Scorpion
cards.note: New card (debate): Drawable animal found in Pakistan. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Staircase
cards.note: New card (debate): Common household noun and different from Ladder. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Sewing Machine
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar object in Pakistani homes. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Scarecrow
cards.note: New card (debate): Easy to act out. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Seesaw
cards.note: New card (debate): Playground item. Not in the deck under either spelling.

cards.Name: Stapler
cards.note: New card (debate): Everyday object. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Sharpener
cards.note: New card (debate): Classic school item. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Sunglasses
cards.note: New card (debate): Different from Glasses and Goggles, and easy to draw. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Stadium
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar to players through cricket. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Tyre
cards.note: New card (debate): Common object, using the local spelling. Different from Wheel and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Waistcoat
cards.note: New card (debate): Common local formalwear that is not in the deck. Adding it keeps Tuxedo. It differs from Vest, which means the baniyan undershirt in Pakistani English.

cards.Name: Rainbow
cards.note: New card (debate): Easy to draw, no content issues, and not in the 1007 live cards.

cards.Name: Umpire
cards.note: New card (debate): Easy to act out with cricket signals. Neither Umpire nor Referee is in the deck.

cards.Name: Wrestler
cards.note: New card (debate): Easy to act out and ties to local pehlwani. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Walnut
cards.note: New card (debate): A familiar dry fruit (akhrot) that is easy to draw. The deck has only the generic 'Nut', so it is not a duplicate.

cards.Name: Well
cards.note: New card (debate): A village well (kuan) is easy to draw and act out. In a Nouns deck it will be read as the noun. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Wheat
cards.note: New card (debate): Pakistan's staple crop (gandum), easy to draw and describe. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Vulture
cards.note: New card (debate): A well-known bird (girh) that is easy to act out. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Valley
cards.note: New card (debate): A landform players know from Hunza and Swat. Not in the deck.

cards.Name: Rehal
cards.note: New card (debate): The Quran stand is a common, drawable item and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Attar
cards.note: New card (debate): The traditional oil perfume, linked to the Sunnah. It is distinct from Perfume and is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Takhti
cards.note: New card (debate): The nostalgic wooden school slate. It is drawable and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Gullak
cards.note: New card (debate): The clay money box found in most Pakistani homes. There is no Piggy Bank or Gullak card.

cards.Name: Charkha
cards.note: New card (debate): The spinning wheel is iconic and easy to act out. Only Spinning Top exists.

cards.Name: Surma
cards.note: New card (debate): Kohl is a Sunnah item and a desi staple. It is distinct from Eyeliner, and there is no Kohl or Kajal card.

cards.Name: Water Tanker
cards.note: New card (debate): A distinctly Pakistani urban truck that is easy to describe. It is not in the deck, and Tank and Truck are different ideas.

cards.Name: Mithai
cards.note: New card (debate): Staple celebration sweets; not in the deck

cards.Name: Sheer Khurma
cards.note: New card (debate): Iconic Eid dish; not in the deck

cards.Name: Chaand Raat
cards.note: New card (debate): Well-known Eid-eve night; not in the deck

cards.Name: Truck Art
cards.note: New card (debate): Distinctly Pakistani and drawable; different from Truck

cards.Name: Bun Kabab
cards.note: New card (debate): Classic street food different from Kebab

cards.Name: Gajra
cards.note: New card (debate): Common jasmine flower bracelet; not in the deck

cards.Name: Peshawari Chappal
cards.note: New card (debate): Famous local footwear, different from Khussa and Sandal

cards.Name: Wuzu
cards.note: New card (debate): Ablution is easy to act out respectfully; common Pakistani spelling; not in the deck

cards.Name: Azaan
cards.note: New card (debate): The call to prayer is universally known to players and is not in the deck; fits Jainamaz/Tasbeeh/Topi

cards.Name: Cricket Ball
cards.note: New card (debate): Only Cricket Bat and Tennis Ball exist; the hard ball is an obvious local noun

cards.Name: Zakat
cards.note: New card (debate): Well-known abstract Islamic noun; no Zakat, Charity or Sadqa card in the deck.

cards.Name: Qibla
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar worship noun; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Hajj
cards.note: New card (debate): Core, very guessable Islamic noun; no Hajj, Umrah or Kaaba card in the deck.

cards.Name: Gulab Jamun
cards.note: New card (debate): Iconic Pakistani sweet that fits with Ladoo and Rasmalai; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Dahi Baray
cards.note: New card (debate): Popular Pakistani street food matching the Golgappa/Chaat set; uses the common Pakistani name rather than the Indian 'Dahi Bhalla'; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Sparrow
cards.note: New card (debate): Common local bird that is easy to draw; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Tubewell
cards.note: New card (debate): Common rural item, different from Hand Pump; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Ihram
cards.note: New card (debate): Accurate Hajj/Umrah garment, concrete and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Zamzam
cards.note: New card (debate): Well-known blessed water from Makkah, not in the deck.

cards.Name: Minbar
cards.note: New card (debate): Masjid pulpit; drawable, familiar, and no existing card covers it.

cards.Name: Bhutta
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar roasted-corn street snack; the deck has no corn-cob card (only Popcorn, Acorn).

cards.Name: Chakki
cards.note: New card (debate): Common flour mill or grinding stone, concrete and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Pitthu Garam
cards.note: New card (debate): Classic Pakistani street game, not in the deck. It complements the existing Gilli Danda and Kabaddi cards.

cards.Name: Sajji
cards.note: New card (debate): Famous Balochi roast dish, not in the deck.

cards.Name: Doli
cards.note: New card (debate): The bride's palanquin at rukhsati; easy to act out and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Walima
cards.note: New card (debate): Sunnah wedding feast familiar to every family, not in the deck.

cards.Name: Aeroplane
cards.note: New card (debate): Common and drawable. Only Toy Plane exists in the deck.

cards.Name: Ant
cards.note: New card (debate): Simple, drawable animal that is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Bee
cards.note: New card (debate): Easy to act out and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Apron
cards.note: New card (debate): Concrete kitchen object that is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Barber
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar person noun alongside Darzi and Dhobi. The deck has no barber, nai or hajjam.

cards.Name: Crab
cards.note: New card (debate): Fun to act out and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Cheetah
cards.note: New card (debate): Well-known animal that is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Bulldozer
cards.note: New card (debate): Concrete machine that is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Calligraphy
cards.note: New card (debate): Culturally fitting Islamic art form that is not in the deck.

cards.Name: Onion
cards.note: New card (debate): Kitchen staple that is easy to act out and not in the deck.

cards.Name: Dua
cards.note: New card (debate): Respectful everyday worship noun that differs from Prayer and is easy to act out; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Fire Extinguisher
cards.note: New card (debate): Concrete object that is easy to act or draw; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Ferris Wheel
cards.note: New card (debate): Familiar mela/park ride that is easy to draw; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Cotton Candy
cards.note: New card (debate): Well-known street treat (buddhi ke baal); no duplicate (only Candy Bar/Wrapper and Cotton Balls/Buds exist).

cards.Name: Dentist
cards.note: New card (debate): Common profession that is fun to act out; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Crutches
cards.note: New card (debate): Concrete object that is easy to act out; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Chimney
cards.note: New card (debate): Easy to draw; not in the deck.

cards.Name: Earphones
cards.note: New card (debate): Everyday object; no Earphone/Headphone card exists.

cards.Name: Chapli Kabab
cards.note: New card (debate): Iconic Peshawari dish that is distinct from the generic Kebab and Bun Kabab cards.

cards.Name: Eagle
cards.note: New card (debate): Well-known animal that is not in the deck (Falcon is a separate card).

cards.Name: Imam
cards.note: New card (debate): A familiar local figure who goes with Masjid, Muezzin and Prayer in the deck. Easy to describe (he leads the jamaat and gives the khutbah).

cards.Name: Hijab
cards.note: New card (debate): An everyday item that is easy to mime and is different from Scarf and Dupatta. Not yet in the deck.

cards.Name: Firefly
cards.note: New card (debate): A drawable, nostalgic noun (jugnu) that is not yet in the deck.

cards.Name: Fingerprint
cards.note: New card (debate): A concrete noun, familiar from NADRA and biometric SIM checks, that is not yet in the deck.

cards.Name: Slingshot
cards.note: New card (debate): The childhood gulel is well known and easy to mime. It is different from Catapult, which is a siege weapon.

cards.Name: Glacier
cards.note: New card (debate): A drawable nature noun with a local link (Siachen, Baltoro) that is not yet in the deck.

cards.Name: Helicopter
cards.note: New card (debate): A very actable vehicle that is missing from the deck (only Toy Plane and Drone are present).

cards.Name: Homework
cards.note: New card (debate): A relatable everyday noun that is not yet in the deck.

cards.Name: Jail
cards.note: New card (debate): An easy-to-act concrete noun. The deck has no Jail or Prison card.

cards.Name: Kitchen
cards.note: New card (debate): A common household place that is easy to describe and is not yet in the deck.

cards.Name: Pothole
cards.note: New card (debate): Checked: not in the deck. A concrete local noun that is easy to act out.

cards.Name: Guest
cards.note: New card (debate): Checked: not in the deck. A central part of desi hospitality and easy to act out.

cards.Name: Neighbour
cards.note: New card (debate): Checked: not in the deck under either spelling. An everyday noun in British spelling.

cards.Name: Mosquito Net
cards.note: New card (debate): A separate everyday object (machhar dani), unlike Mosquito or Mosquito Coil. Compound nouns already appear in the deck.

cards.Name: Nazar
cards.note: New card (debate): Checked: not in the deck, and no Evil Eye card exists. The owner explicitly allows nazar jokes.

cards.Name: Policeman
cards.note: New card (debate): Checked: no police card in the deck. A familiar person noun that is easy to act out.

cards.Name: Monsoon
